label: Heavy social-media user with elevated loneliness, depression, and anxiety symptoms
summary: This profile is characterized by comparatively higher loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms, alongside heavier daily social-media use. It represents respondents with above-average emotional distress indicators and high time spent on social platforms.
demographic_anchor: Female respondent with graduate-level education or above and more than 5 hours of daily social-media use.
behavior_markers: Reports comparatively higher loneliness levels
Shows elevated depressive symptom scores
Shows elevated anxiety symptom scores
Spends heavy amounts of time on social media each day
Daily social-media use is centered around a high-use range
tone: Distressed, socially immersed, and emotionally burdened

label: Low-distress, light social-media user
summary: Respondents in this profile report comparatively low loneliness, very low depressive symptoms, very low anxiety symptoms, and relatively light daily social-media use.
demographic_anchor: Typically male, with graduate-level education or higher, and about 1–3 hours of daily social-media use.
behavior_markers: Reports lower loneliness than higher-distress profiles
Shows low average depressive symptom levels
Shows very low average anxiety symptom levels
Uses social media for a relatively limited amount of time each day
Daily social-media use centers around the light-use range
tone: Stable, low-distress, and moderate in digital engagement

label: Socially connected but heavy-use women
summary: Women in this profile report comparatively higher loneliness alongside lower average depressive and anxiety symptoms, and they spend relatively long periods on social media each day.
demographic_anchor: Typically female, educated to graduate level or above, with about 3-5 hours of daily social-media use.
behavior_markers: Reports relatively elevated loneliness compared with other measured symptoms.
Shows lower average depressive symptoms.
Shows lower average anxiety symptoms.
Uses social media heavily on a daily basis, averaging close to five hours per day.
Represents a mid-sized subgroup in the training split (n=167).
tone: Emotionally somewhat isolated but not broadly distressed, with frequent daily engagement on social media.

label: Low-distress light social-media user
summary: Respondents in this profile report comparatively low loneliness, low depressive symptoms, and low anxiety symptoms, alongside lighter daily social-media use.
demographic_anchor: Typically male, educated to graduate level or above, and using social media about 1–3 hours per day.
behavior_markers: Reports low average loneliness (UCLA-8 mean 1.22).
Shows low average depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 mean 0.82).
Shows low average anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean 0.90).
Uses social media relatively lightly, with an average daily midpoint of about 1.61 hours.
Represents a training-split subgroup of 217 respondents.
tone: Stable, low-distress, and moderate in daily digital engagement.
